theory.overview: A Bloom Filter is a space-efficient probabilistic data structure used to test whether an element is a member of a set. It may return false positives (says element is in set when it's not) but never false negatives (if it says not in set, definitely not in set). Uses multiple hash functions to set bits in a bit array. Insertion and lookup are O(k) where k is number of hash functions. Bloom filters are used in databases (Cassandra, HBase), CDNs, cryptocurrency, and network routing.

keyConcepts.name: Probabilistic Membership
keyConcepts.description: Can tell 'possibly in set' or 'definitely not in set'. False positive rate can be tuned by size and hash count.

keyConcepts.name: Multiple Hash Functions
keyConcepts.description: Element is hashed by k independent hash functions. Each hash sets/checks a different bit position.

keyConcepts.name: Space Efficiency
keyConcepts.description: Only stores ~10 bits per element regardless of element size. 1% false positive with 10 bits per element.

keyConcepts.name: No Deletion
keyConcepts.description: Standard Bloom filters don't support deletion. Counting Bloom Filters use counters instead of bits to enable deletion.

complexity.insert: O(k) where k = number of hash functions
complexity.falsePositive: ≈ (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k where m = bits, n = elements

algorithmSteps.description: Insert 'hello': hash1=2, hash2=5, hash3=8. Set bits 2,5,8 to 1
Insert 'world': hash1=1, hash2=5, hash3=9. Set bits 1,5,9 to 1. Bit 5 already 1.
Lookup 'hello': check bits 2,5,8. All are 1 → 'MAYBE in set' (possibly true)
Lookup 'test': check bits 0,3,7. Bit 3=0 → 'DEFINITELY NOT in set' (no false negatives)
Lookup 'xyz': hashes point to bits 1,5,9 (all set by hello/world). FALSE POSITIVE!
